source: Açık PPL soru listeleri (Austro Control ECQB-PPL(A) 80 AGK özeti v2015.4; Traficom PPL020) bankayla tek tek karşılaştırıldı (2026-11-17). Bankada hiçbir biçimde sorulmayan, ders notunda geçen, şekil gerektirmeyen bilgiler; metin bağımsız yazıldı.
answer_convention: Doğru cevap ilk şıktır (A). Sunum katmanı şıkları karıştırır.
id_convention: 52204 ve 52211+ bandı: başka açık bankalarda olup bizde olmayan 020 soruları. Mevcut ve emekli kimlikler yeniden kullanılmaz.
ecqb_eslesme: 162 sorudan 35'i alındı. 101, 54, 58, 64, 149 → 52211–52215; 46, 50, 51, 27, 72, 89, 62 → 52216–52222; 8→52223, 14→52224, 18→52225, 22→52226, 25→52227, 48→52228, 52→52229, 56→52230, 57→52231, 70→52232, 78→52233, 85→52234, 92→52235, 132→52236, 133→52237, 137→52238, 138→52239, 148→52240, 150→52241, 151→52242, 153→52243, 154→52244, 155→52245, 158→52246 (kullanıcı 2026-11-17'de 'bizde olmayan bütün soruları ekle' dedi; aynı konunun başka yönü/sayısı artık eleme nedeni değil); 53 → 52201 (020-SH). Traficom 150 → 52204. Kalanlar bankada aynı soru+aynı cevap olarak var ya da alınmadı: şekilli sorular (4, 7, 16–21, 26, 59–61, 82–83; çizimleri yok), çelişkili anahtar (41–42: ECQB burun-ağır/kuyruk-ağır trimde tab yönünü fiziğe ve 14479'a ters veriyor; 69: oktan = tutuşma sıcaklığı, 66'daki 'vuruntu direnci' ile çelişiyor).

questions.text: In the ISA near mean sea level, a change of 1 hPa in the altimeter subscale setting changes the indicated altitude by approximately:
options: 27 ft
3 ft
100 ft
270 ft

questions.text: What is the purpose of the altimeter subscale (pressure setting window)?
options: To refer the altimeter reading to a selected pressure level such as QNH, QFE or 1013.25 hPa
To correct the altimeter reading for non-standard temperature
To correct the instrument and hysteresis errors of the altimeter
To set the reference altitude of the transponder's altitude encoder

questions.text: The alternator of a light aircraft fails in flight. What is the immediate effect?
options: Little change at first: the battery supplies the electrical system until it is discharged
The engine stops, because the magnetos are powered by the alternator
The altimeter and airspeed indicator stop working at once
The battery is immediately disconnected and all electrical equipment fails

questions.text: Which cylinder arrangement is most common in the piston engines of light aircraft?
options: Horizontally opposed (boxer)
In-line
V
Radial

questions.text: Where does condensed water collect in an aircraft fuel tank, and how is it removed?
options: At the lowest point of the tank, from where it is drained through the drain valve
On the surface of the fuel, from where it evaporates through the tank vent
Evenly mixed through the fuel, so it can only be removed by filtering
At the top of the tank, near the filler cap

questions.text: On an airspeed indicator, what does the yellow arc mark?
options: The caution range, to be used only in smooth air (from VNO up to VNE)
The normal operating range
The flap operating range
The speed that must never be exceeded

questions.text: What is the primer of a light aircraft piston engine?
options: A small hand-operated pump that sprays fuel into the intake before starting, to make the engine easier to start
A lever that engages the turbocharger
A valve in the carburettor that adjusts the mixture automatically
The nozzle in the carburettor venturi that atomises the fuel

questions.text: In which unit is electrical voltage expressed?
options: Volt
Ampere
Ohm
Watt

questions.text: In which unit is electrical power expressed?
options: Watt
Volt
Ampere
Ohm

questions.text: About how many axes does an aircraft move in flight?
What is a typical consequence of carburettor icing?
options: A loss of engine power
An increase in engine power
A drop in oil pressure
A rise in oil pressure

questions.text: During the ignition grounding check the ignition switch is moved briefly to OFF and then back to BOTH. If the ignition system is correctly grounded, what happens to the RPM?
options: It drops when OFF is selected and returns to the previous value when BOTH is selected again
It rises when OFF is selected and returns to the previous value when BOTH is selected again
It does not change, because the magnetos keep firing until the engine stops
It drops when OFF is selected and stays below the previous value when BOTH is selected again

questions.text: During the magneto check the engine runs unusually rough on one magneto. What is the most likely cause?
options: A defective (e.g. fouled) spark plug
The starter is still engaged
The fuel tank vent is blocked
The alternator has failed

questions.text: A sandwich structure consists of:
options: Two thin load-bearing face sheets and a light supporting core
Two thick supporting face sheets and a light load-bearing core
Two thin supporting face sheets and a heavy supporting core
Two thick supporting face sheets and a heavy load-bearing core

questions.text: Dents or wrinkles found in the airframe structure may indicate:
options: A hard landing or overstressing of the structure
Material defects or old paint
Heavy erosion or wear
Excessive engine RPM and a cylinder defect

questions.text: What is a disadvantage of retractable landing gear?
options: Higher weight
More drag in flight
Higher fuel consumption
Higher approach speed

questions.text: What can compromise the static strength of the airframe?
options: Exceeding the manoeuvring speed in strong gusts
A stall caused by too high an angle of attack
Trimming out the control forces for the flight condition
Flying below a certain airspeed

questions.text: Which control is connected to the nose-wheel or tail-wheel steering?
options: Rudder
Aileron
Elevator
Trim tab

questions.text: Unless the flight manual says otherwise, what should be done before switching to another fuel tank in an aircraft with an electric auxiliary fuel pump?
options: Switch the auxiliary fuel pump on
Switch the ignition off
Apply carburettor heat
Use the primer

questions.text: What does a voltmeter indicate?
options: Voltage
Current
Electrical power
Resistance

questions.text: How are instruments that are powered by the aircraft's electrical system marked?
options: "DC"
"EL"
"CO"
"AL"

questions.text: Which equipment may be affected by a failure of the aircraft's electrical system?
options: Radios, radio navigation equipment and electrically driven gyro instruments
Radios, radio navigation equipment and the magnetic compass
Fuel quantity indication, radios and the altimeter
Airspeed indicator, altimeter and vacuum-driven attitude indicator

questions.text: On a run-up with a fixed-pitch propeller, what is the immediate effect of applying carburettor heat?
options: The RPM drops
The RPM rises
The propeller blade angle increases
The propeller blade angle decreases

questions.text: What happens when the engine oil filter becomes clogged?
options: A bypass valve opens: oil keeps circulating, but it is no longer filtered
A bypass valve opens and a spare filter takes over
Oil circulation stops after about 30 minutes
Oil circulation stops after about 15 minutes

questions.text: Unless the flight manual says otherwise, how should power be reduced with a constant-speed propeller?
options: First reduce manifold pressure, then reduce RPM
First reduce RPM, then reduce manifold pressure
First reduce manifold pressure, then increase RPM
First reduce RPM, then increase manifold pressure

questions.text: How must the fuel quantity be indicated?
options: Each tank has its own gauge, which reads zero when only unusable fuel remains in level flight
One calibrated gauge for all tanks is sufficient
Each tank has its own gauge, which reads zero when 20 minutes of fuel remain
Each tank has two independent gauges, one of which triggers a warning light

questions.text: An aircraft in the northern hemisphere accelerates on a magnetic heading of 270°. During the acceleration the magnetic compass indicates approximately:
An aircraft in the northern hemisphere decelerates on a magnetic heading of 270°. During the deceleration the magnetic compass indicates approximately:
How does a freely spinning gyroscope respond to an applied force?
options: It reacts at a point displaced 90° in the direction of rotation (precession)
It moves in the same direction as the force
It reacts at a point displaced 45°
It turns towards north

questions.text: The apparent drift of a directional gyro (caused by the earth's rotation) is:
options: 15°/h × sin(latitude)
13°/h × sin(latitude)
15°/h × cos(longitude)
13°/h × cos(longitude)

questions.text: What does the abbreviation ADI stand for?
options: Attitude Director Indicator
Advanced Directional Indicator
Attitude Deviation Indication
Aircraft De-Icing

questions.text: An Attitude Director Indicator (ADI) combines the indications of:
options: The attitude indicator and the flight director
The directional gyro and the turn indicator
The attitude indicator and the radio compass (RBI)
The directional gyro and the VOR indicator (OBI)

questions.text: A Horizontal Situation Indicator (HSI) combines the indications of:
options: The directional gyro and the VOR indicator
The attitude indicator and the flight director
The turn indicator and the slip ball
The directional gyro and the flight director

questions.text: Among other things, the Primary Flight Display (PFD) of an EFIS can show:
options: Attitude, heading, VOR radial or approach course, flight director
Navigation information, bearings to several stations, ATC flight plan
Oil pressure and temperature, cylinder head and exhaust gas temperatures
ATC flight plan and CPDLC messages

questions.text: Among other things, the Navigation Display (ND) of an EFIS can show:
options: Navigation information, bearings to several stations, the flight plan route
Attitude, heading, VOR radial or approach course, flight director
Oil pressure and temperature, cylinder head and exhaust gas temperatures
ATC flight plan and CPDLC messages

questions.text: The altimeter subscale is changed from 1000 hPa to 1010 hPa. How does the indication change?
options: It reads about 80 m (270 ft) more than before
It reads about 80 m less than before
It depends on the QNH
It does not change

questions.text: If the expansion chamber (capacity flask) of a variometer is too large, the variometer will:
options: Over-read
Under-read
Show nothing
Be heavily stressed
